Hi Ben —

Thanks for the invite. When I click the Meet link I get an error: "You need permission to join this meeting. Contact the organizer."

We're on a locked-down G Suite domain and our security team restricts external organizers for meetings that include internal staff. I suspect the problem is the calendar organizer was created under an external account (our tenant blocks that). Could you confirm who created the invite?

Quick workaround if easier — can you send a Zoom link? Our team can join Zoom without the same organizer restriction.

Samir

Hi Samir —

Sorry for the friction here. I checked the calendar: the invite was generated by Ben but as a calendar event forwarded from a test account, which sometimes causes the guest to be marked as the organizer on other G Suite tenants. We see this behavior when invites are created while an external calendar is the active calendar — the organizer field in the ICS points to a non-Redwood address and some domains block join.

Options:
- I can create a fresh event in my Redwood calendar (I will be the organizer) and re-send. That should remove the permission block.
- If you prefer not to accept a new Meet event, Ben can create a Zoom meeting and we’ll send a fallback invite (less friction for most enterprise tenants).

Marcus: FYI — we saw a similar blocker with TruTech two months ago; I remember we had to recreate the event instead of editing the original.

Ben — can you confirm which you prefer? If we recreate the Meet event I’ll make sure the organizer is lauren.bishop@redwood.com. If Zoom, Ben, please send an alternative link and we’ll attach a new ICS with Lauren as organizer where possible.

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
